title: The 10 Best Stand Mixers for Bread
h1: The 10 Best Stand Mixers for Bread
metaDescription: Our 10 picks for stand mixers for bread, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at stand mixers for bread using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: KitchenAid KP26M1XER Professional 600 Series 6-Qt. Bowl-Lift
products.blurb: Key specs: 575W motor with bowl-lift design, 6-quart stainless bowl, Spiral dough hook, flat beater, and wire whip included.
strengths: Bowl-lift design holds the bowl rigid against a yoke, eliminating the tilt-head flex that develops under repeated heavy dough
575W motor sustains 10-minute kneading cycles without the warm-up pauses smaller tilt-head motors need
Spiral dough hook centers dough automatically instead of pushing it to one side of the bowl
6-quart bowl handles two standard loaves or one large artisan batch per cycle
limitations: 17+ inch height does not fit under most upper cabinets
Bowl-lift mechanism is slower to load and unload than a tilt-head for quick single-item tasks
features: Spiral dough hook, flat beater, and wire whip included

products.name: Bosch Universal Plus Stand Mixer MUM6N10UC
products.blurb: Key specs: 500W motor with bowl-drive (motor-in-base) mechanism, 6.5-quart stainless bowl, holds 8 cups of flour, Spiral dough hook, balloon whisk, and cookie paddles included.
strengths: Motor-in-base layout delivers the highest usable kneading torque of any consumer stand mixer
Handles 8-pound flour batches, four standard loaves, in a single continuous cycle
Bowl-drive geometry eliminates dough-climbing up the hook shaft, a common head-drive problem
Costs less than a comparable KitchenAid bowl-lift despite more raw power
limitations: Attachment ecosystem is much smaller than KitchenAid's
Covered bowl makes adding ingredients mid-mix less intuitive than a tilt-head
1-year limited warranty versus KitchenAid's longer coverage
features: 6.5-quart stainless bowl, holds 8 cups of flour
Spiral dough hook, balloon whisk, and cookie paddles included
Motor-in-base design maximizes torque without head leverage limits

products.name: Breville BEM825BAL the Bakery Chef Stand Mixer
products.blurb: Key specs: 550W motor with electronic speed sensor that maintains speed under load, 5-quart stainless bowl with bowl-lift design, Built-in scale for measuring ingredients directly in the bowl.
strengths: Electronic speed sensor actively compensates for dough resistance, holding a set speed rather than bogging down like standard AC motors
Integrated scale removes a separate measuring step for flour and liquids
Bowl-lift stability with a lower profile than most bowl-lift competitors
limitations: Breville's attachment lineup for this model is limited compared to KitchenAid's hub ecosystem
Price sits at a premium similar to KitchenAid's bowl-lift models without the same brand recognition for baking
features: 550W motor with electronic speed sensor that maintains speed under load
Built-in scale for measuring ingredients directly in the bowl

products.name: KitchenAid KSM70SKXX 7-Qt. Bowl-Lift Stand Mixer
products.blurb: Key specs: 800W motor with bowl-lift design, 7-quart stainless bowl, Spiral dough hook, flat beater, and wire whip included.
strengths: 7-quart bowl handles triple batches or three standard loaves in one cycle, the largest practical capacity in the KitchenAid consumer lineup
800W motor keeps pace with large dense-dough batches that would tax a 6-quart bowl-lift
Spiral dough hook centers large dough masses consistently across the bigger bowl diameter
limitations: Large footprint and height make storage and under-cabinet placement difficult
Overkill capacity for single-loaf or small-batch bakers
Price sits near the top of the consumer stand mixer range
features: Spiral dough hook, flat beater, and wire whip included

products.name: KitchenAid KSM150PSER Artisan 5-Qt. Tilt-Head Stand Mixer
products.blurb: Key specs: 325W continuous-rated motor with 10-speed control, 5-quart stainless bowl, tilt-head design, C-hook dough hook, flat beater, and wire whisk included.
strengths: Handles standard single-loaf bread recipes without difficulty at speed 2
Tilt-head design is faster to load for a single weekly loaf than a bowl-lift
Attachment hub opens the door to a pasta roller or grinder without buying a second machine
limitations: 325W motor and C-hook are not built for double-loaf batches or frequent heavy dough use
Motor runs warm after 4 to 5 minutes of continuous stiff-dough kneading
Tilt-head latch can develop slight play under years of repeated bread stress
features: C-hook dough hook, flat beater, and wire whisk included
Compatible with 12+ official KitchenAid hub attachments

products.name: Cuisinart SM-70 7-Qt. 12-Speed Stand Mixer
products.blurb: Key specs: 500W motor with bowl-lift design, 7-quart stainless bowl, 12 speeds.
strengths: 7-quart bowl-lift stability at a lower price than KitchenAid's equivalent bowl-lift models
500W motor handles large dough batches without the strain a tilt-head at this wattage would show
12 speeds give finer low-end control for gentle bread-starter mixing than most bowl-lift competitors
limitations: Cuisinart's attachment ecosystem for the SM-70 hub is far smaller than KitchenAid's
Bowl-lift height still requires open counter clearance above the machine
features: Dough hook, flat beater, and whisk included

products.name: KitchenAid KSMC895 Commercial Series 8-Qt. Bowl-Lift
products.blurb: Key specs: 1.3 HP commercial-rated motor with bowl-lift design, 8-quart stainless bowl, Spiral dough hook rated for continuous commercial-style use.
strengths: 1.3 HP commercial motor is rated for continuous use well beyond household duty cycles
8-quart bowl and spiral hook handle the largest home or small-commercial dough batches without motor strain
NSF certification signals build quality appropriate for near-daily heavy bread production
limitations: Price and footprint are excessive for anyone baking less than several times per week
No practical benefit over the 6-quart Pro 600 for households making one to two loaves at a time
features: 1.3 HP commercial-rated motor with bowl-lift design
Spiral dough hook rated for continuous commercial-style use

products.name: Cuisinart SM-50BCC 5.5-Qt. 12-Speed Stand Mixer
products.blurb: Key specs: 500W motor with 12-speed control, 5.5-quart stainless bowl, tilt-head design, Die-cast zinc body with lever-lock tilt-head.
strengths: 500W motor outperforms the KitchenAid Artisan on stiff dough and bagel batches at a lower price
5.5-quart bowl handles a double-loaf batch that a 5-quart tilt-head cannot
Lever-lock tilt-head holds position more firmly under dough stress than a spring latch
limitations: Tilt-head design still develops flex over years of heavy repeated bread use, same as any tilt-head
Smaller attachment ecosystem than KitchenAid limits future expansion
features: Die-cast zinc body with lever-lock tilt-head

products.name: KitchenAid KSM8990OB Commercial 8-Qt. Stand Mixer (Onyx Black)
products.blurb: Key specs: 1.3 HP commercial motor with bowl-lift design, 8-quart stainless bowl in onyx black finish, Spiral dough hook rated for continuous use.
strengths: Commercial-rated motor and NSF certification suit dedicated home bakers producing bread multiple times weekly
8-quart capacity matches the largest batches most home ovens can bake in one session
Onyx black finish distinguishes it visually from the standard commercial silver models
limitations: Large size and weight make it a permanent counter fixture, not a stored appliance
Price is not justified for anyone baking fewer than several loaves per week
features: 1.3 HP commercial motor with bowl-lift design
8-quart stainless bowl in onyx black finish
Spiral dough hook rated for continuous use

products.name: KitchenAid KSM3311XBM Artisan Mini 3.5-Qt.
products.blurb: Key specs: 250W motor with 10-speed control, 3.5-quart stainless bowl, tilt-head design, C-hook dough hook, flat beater, and wire whisk included.
strengths: Full KitchenAid attachment compatibility in a compact 3.5-quart body, no functional attachment downgrade versus the 5-quart Artisan
250W motor handles a single standard loaf (3 cups flour) without strain
Smaller footprint suits kitchens without room for a full-size stand mixer
limitations: 3.5-quart bowl caps out well below a full loaf-and-a-half batch
250W motor is the least powerful in the KitchenAid consumer lineup, not for double batches or stiff dough
Not the right choice for households baking more than one loaf at a time
features: C-hook dough hook, flat beater, and wire whisk included
Compatible with the full KitchenAid attachment hub
20% smaller footprint than the full-size Artisan

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
